title: VPC tenant commissioning and handoff playbook
author: Marco Chen
body:
Summary:

This playbook describes a repeatable, audit-friendly process to commission a new VPC tenant for Redwood Private deployments and perform the field operational handoff to the customer's Platform/Ops team. It covers pre-commissioning checks, zero-touch bootstrapping, acceptance/validation tests, automated evidence capture for compliance, and an explicit handoff checklist.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Field engineers, solutions engineers, customer SRE/Platform operators, and professional services technical leads.
- Scope: VPC-hosted Private deployments (control plane managed, runtime in customer VPC). Does NOT cover fully air-gapped on‑prem appliances (see onprem packaging docs).

Goals:
- Provide deterministic steps for tenant provisioning, network wiring, and validation.
- Ensure on-the-books evidence for security/compliance review (KMS/HSM integration, firewall policy proofs, TLS cert artifacts).
- Minimize manual interventions via templated bootstrap configs and zero-touch secrets exchange.

Pre-commissioning prerequisites (verify before scheduling build):
1) Customer commitment and contract: signed SOW with region and capacity targets, IP allowlist and responsible contacts.
2) Network readiness checklist (all must be green):
   - VPC CIDR ranges reserved and documented.
   - BGP or Direct Connect circuits confirmed (if using cross-region failover).
   - Subnets created: control-plane-subnet, runtime-subnet-1..N, mgmt-subnet.
   - Egress NAT / routing strategy documented and security groups prepared.
3) IAM & KMS preparatory steps:
   - Customer KMS key created for model payloads and telemetry encryption (key id).
   - Service account (rwd-deploy-agent) created with least-privilege IAM policy.
   - HSM/KMS onboarding ticket completed if required.
4) Hardware and capacity: GPU instance types reserved per capacity profile; ephemeral and persistent storage quotas verified.
5) Observability contract: target sampling rates, retention window, and endpoint URIs for obs-collector must be provided.
6) Access and credentials: field-team SSH bastion user, jump host details, SAML/OIDC integration plan.

Commissioning timeline (recommended):
- T-minus 48 hours: validate prerequisites and share bootstrap bundle.
- Day 0 (build): perform automated bootstrap and runtime image provisioning.
- Day 1 (validation): run smoke, SLA tests, telemetry verification, and acceptance tests.
- Day 2 (handoff): operational training, transfer runbook, and sign-off.

Step-by-step commissioning procedure:
1) Generate tenant bootstrap bundle (field engineer)
   - Action: from redwood CLI, generate a tenant bundle that includes: tenant id, model manifest subset, quantization profile, runtime node profile, and signed KMS metadata.
   - Example command:

     rwdctl tenant create --name "acme-corp-east" --region us-east-1 --capacity profile:small --output tenant-bundle-acme.tar.gz

   - Deliverable: tenant-bundle-acme.tar.gz (signed, contains checksums and a signed policy.json).

2) Zero-touch provisioning (operator)
   - Upload bundle to customer staging bucket (instructions in vendor-handoff package).
   - On the customer's provisioning host, run the deploy agent bootstrap:

     sudo rwd-agent bootstrap --bundle /tmp/tenant-bundle-acme.tar.gz 

   - The agent performs: node registration with redwood-control-plane, pulls runtime images, applies kernel-level tuning (NUMA, CUDA settings), and starts runtime services: rwd-runtime, kv-cache-service, rwd-metrics-forwarder.

3) Automated verification suite (CI-style):
   - Run smoke tests (expect pass)
     - healthcheck /api/v1/health -> 200 within 3s
     - kv-cache warmup and eviction exercise -> within target throughput
   - Latency profile run (synthetic):
     - 1000 requests synthetic workload through rwd-proxy over 10 minutes; p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms (small profile targets).
   - Cost and batching validation: ensure batching achieves configured tokens/second or provide recommended adjustments.

4) Security and KMS validation:
   - Verify envelope encryption: decrypt a small test blob using customer KMS key to prove integration.
   - TLS: verify mTLS between rwd-agent and control-plane using deployed certs.
   - Firewall proof: capture iptables/nsg-config export and sign it into evidence bundle.

Acceptance criteria (must be signed-off by both Redwood and customer SRE):
- Functional: all runtime services in Ready state; model load success on at least one replica.
- Performance: synthetic latency and throughput tests meet profile targets within +-10%.
- Reliability: readiness/ liveness probes pass for 30 minutes under light synthetic traffic.
- Security: KMS test decrypt succeeded; certificate chain verified; all required ports are closed except allowed list.
- Observability: metrics and traces appear in customer obs endpoint with correct tenant tag and sampling rate.

Acceptance evidence artifacts (automatically captured where possible):
- healthcheck.log (timestamped)
- latency-run-YYYYMMDD.json (latency histogram)
- bootstrap-manifest.json (signed)
- kms-integration-test.out
- iptables-or-nsg-export.txt
- metrics-sample-YYYYMMDD.ndjson

Operational handoff checklist (to be completed during Day 2 session):
- Transfer documentation: runtime runbooks, node repair instructions, poc for kv-cache reset.
- Access handover: ensure customer owners have admin access to the control plane portal and rwdctl.
- Alerting: confirm alerts are mirrored into customer pager/SRE tools (PagerDuty/JiraOps).
- Escalation tree: provide 24/7 on-call SLAs per contract (include names/emails/phone).
- Runbooks: ensure customer has local copies of runbooks and the automated recovery scripts.

Runbook highlights (copy these commands into the customer-runbook):
- Restart runtime service (safe restart):

  sudo systemctl restart rwd-runtime
  # Wait for readiness: rwdctl node status --node-id <id> --watch

- Flush KV cache (safe mode):

  rwdctl kv flush --tenant acme-corp-east --graceful

- Swap model to lower-cost variant (for degradation):

  rwdctl model rollback --tenant acme-corp-east --model-id rwd-llama-13b-q4 --target rwd-llama-13b-int8
Rollback and upgrade safety matrix:
- If a canary upgrade fails health checks within 15 minutes: immediately trigger rollback via rwdctl rollout rollback --canary-id <id>.
- If kv-cache migration causes evictions beyond threshold (20% mem-pressure): pause migration, revert to previous snapshot, and notify Redwood-runbooks.
- For control plane partial outages, activate standby region routing policy as documented in cross-region-failover runbook.

Automated evidence collection (recommended):
- Use the rwd-ops-evidence tool to bundle verification artifacts into an encrypted evidence tarball:

  rwd-ops-evidence collect --tenant acme-corp-east --output evidence-acme-20260310.tar.gz

Telemetry & observability contract (what to confirm during commissioning):
- Metrics: token rate, inference latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU util, memory pressure, KV hit/miss rate.
- Traces: capture at least one end-to-end trace per successful request with tenant id and model id tags.
- Logs: structured JSON logs, level=info for normal ops, level=warn for retries, level=error for failures.
- Retention and sampling: confirm customer retention (30 days default) and sampling (1% traces default, adjusted for regulated customers).

Security & compliance notes:
- Secrets lifecycle: explain key rotation cadence (recommended 90 days), revocation procedure (revoke, replace, rotate), and emergency key rotation play.
- Evidence for auditors: checklist of artifacts (KMS logs, cert snapshots, firewall configs) and how to export them.

Ownership and contacts (example):
- Field lead (Redwood): Marco Chen, marco@redwood.ai, +1-415-555-0114
- Solutions Engineering: Priya Nair, priya@redwood.ai
- Customer primary SRE: <customer-sre-name> (populate during onboarding)
- Escalation on-call (Redwood): ops-escalation@redwood.ai (24/7)

Common failure modes and mitigation recipes:
- Node fails to register: check rwd-agent logs (/var/log/rwd-agent.log) for certificate error; verify certificate TTL and system clock sync (ntp).
- High cold-start latency after bootstrap: validate that model shards are colocated on GPU nodes and that prefetching is enabled in bootstrap manifest.
- Observability not arriving downstream: ensure outbound egress whitelist contains obs-collector FQNs and TLS termination is allowed.

Appendix A — Example minimal tenant bootstrap manifest (YAML):

  tenant_id: acme-corp-east
  region: us-east-1
  capacity_profile: small
  runtime_profiles:
    - node_type: g5.12xlarge
      replicas: 2
  models:
    - id: rwd-llama-13b-q4
      pinned: true
  quant_profiles:
    - name: default-q4
  kms_key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcdef01-2345-6789-abcd-ef0123456789
  telemetry_endpoint: https://obs-customer.acme.internal/ingest

Appendix B — Acceptance test matrix (short form):
- Functional tests: healthcheck, model load, inference correctness (pass/fail).
- Performance: p50, p95 targets per capacity_profile.
- Security: KMS decrypt, cert chain validation.

Sign-off template (fill and e-mail to ops@redwood.ai and customer-sre):
- "I, <name>, on behalf of <customer>, accept the Tenant Commissioning for acme-corp-east. All acceptance tests passed and artifacts uploaded to evidence-acme-20260310.tar.gz."

References and related artifacts:
- control-plane onboarding API guide (internal link)
- private-deploy-operator-cheat-sheet (internal link)
- evidence collection CLI docs

Notes and improvements backlog (observed during iteration):
- Add a lightweight synthetic generator pre-seed to reduce cold-starts when model shards are large.
- Automate KMS integration test to run during the bootstrap and auto-attach results to evidence bundle.

End of playbook.
